question.problem: Find the curvature of the curve $y=\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ at $x=\pi .$
question.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(x)$ of a plane curve $y=y(x)$ is given by

$$
κ(x)=\frac{|{y}^{″}(x)|}{(1+[{y}^{′}(x)]^{2})^{3/2}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${y}^{′}(x)$ and ${y}^{″}(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x,\, & {y}^{″}(x) & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these into the formula for the curvature, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(x) & =\frac{|-\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x|}{{[1+{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}^{2}]}^{3/2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature at $x=\pi $ is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\pi ) & =\frac{|-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi -\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi |}{{[1+{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi +\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi )}^{2}]}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{|1-0|}{{[1+(0+1)^{2}]}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
